title: When the Interval Is Smaller Than the Instrument: code and analysis for two failure modes of streaming latency benchmarks

creators.name: Ricou, Gustavo Pedro
creators.affiliation: School of Computer Science and Statistics, Trinity College Dublin, Dublin, Ireland

description:
Code, analysis and manuscript for a study of two failure modes of sub-millisecond streaming latency benchmarking, both governed by one ratio: the instrument's timescale over the interval being measured.

Mode A (inversion): cross-process latency is a two-clock difference and cannot be negative; applied to every run, that check rejected 1,321 of 2,266, including every run behind a statistically clean result we were about to publish. The mechanism is scheduling, not clock skew, established by manipulation: real-time priority on the stamping threads collapses the inversion rate by 39x and 54x at fixed utilisation, and two core geometries at identical utilisation differ by 2.07x.

Mode B (deletion): the OpenMessaging Benchmark silently deletes every sample whose millisecond-quantised difference is not positive. Across 223 instrumented runs it computed its reported distribution from 0.36% to 100% of the samples it took, reporting the same median either way. Retention obeys a grid law in the reduced fraction of send interval over timestamp quantum, confirmed by a pre-registered payload manipulation, reproduced by a 200-line Python harness with no JVM, and measured across two clocks. The sign channel caught 41,403 genuine one-tick causality violations being absorbed by the same guard.

What changed in v2.5. The manuscript is retargeted at IEEE Transactions on Computers (IEEEtran, 12 pages, 45 references, with the supplement compiled from the same commit) and has been through seven further rounds of adversarial internal review. The substantive changes: (1) Mode B's mathematics is set against its prior art — Hewlett-Packard Application Note 162-1 (1970) owns the retention identity and the 1/q averaging ceiling, and IEEE Std 1241's coherent-sampling condition owns the coprimality lemma; what this work claims is the consequence under deletion. (2) An audited-harness registry: seven benchmarking tools across four languages and seven vendors read at source, with class labels recomputed on every build by the same classifier that read the OpenMessaging Benchmark; five dispose of an inverted or sub-quantum sample silently (filter, substitution, or a library refusal the caller never checks) and two are counterexamples — Rezolus counts its discards, and emqtt-bench keeps every sample, a correction of our own earlier misreading that the supplement records in print. (3) The clock-incoherence rival is closed twice: the platform probe's 90 ns observable increment bounds the testbed clocksource to kvm-clock or tsc, both cross-vCPU coherent, and the corpus closes it again on headroom — the deepest inversion (−99.8 ms) is 455× larger than the send-referenced span's floor (+220 µs over 5,913 runs, which never inverts). (4) The traced stall spectrum is reported as trimodal, with the 2–4 ms mode holding 10.5% of wakeups attributed to the EEVDF base slice (0.75 ms × 4 on kernel 6.8, the maintainers' own arithmetic), refuting a power-law reading: two estimators of one index differ sixfold and a bootstrap goodness-of-fit rejects at p < 0.0004. (5) Every claim the manuscript makes about third-party source or standards — about ninety items — was re-verified at source, and the two errors found were corrected in the text with the verification gates added to the suite, which now carries 2,501 tests including PDF-compliance, cross-document pointer, and registry-vocabulary checks.

The archive contains the instrumentation, every campaign script and ledger, the analysis suite that recomputes the manuscript's numbers from committed data and fails if paper and data disagree, the manuscript, and its supplement.

Data note. No StatsBomb event data is redistributed. Replay plans derived from it are excluded from this record and regenerable byte-for-byte from a pinned upstream commit with the included scripts.
